newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: Slovakia appeals to join NATO with neighbours.
newsitem.headline: Slovakia appeals to join NATO with neighbours.

text.p: Slovakia, facing criticism for its treatment of minorities, appealed on Thursday to be included in the first wave of ex-communist states destined to join the NATO military alliance next year.

Slovak Foreign Minister Pavol Hamzik told the Organisation for Security and Cooperation in Europe (OSCE) that it was crucial for the stability of central Europe that Slovakia join NATO along with its neighbours, Poland, the Czech Republic and Hungary.
"The Slovak Republic still finds itself in...an inconvenient and historically risky security vacuum," Hamzik said in a speech to the OSCE's Vienna-based permanent council.
"We are convinced that only the inclusion of the Slovak Republic into the community of developed democratic states is a guarantee of our security," he added.
Hamzik said Slovakia, through its history, culture and Christian ideals, was a natural part of Western civilisation.
"We do not want to be a bridge to the East...The Slovak Republic has an eminent interest in joining NATO in the first wave along with our neighbours," he said.
Poland, Hungary and the Czech Republic have been practically assured a place in NATO, probably next year. Slovenia has also been mooted as a possible member.

The inclusion of Slovakia in the 16-member Atlantic alliance as early as next year appears to have stalled amid growing concern over the treatment of its minorities, in particular the 600,000-strong ethnic Hungarian community.
NATO and the European Union insist that former East Bloc countries must settle disputes with their neighbours before having any chance of being accepted into the two organisations.

The U.S. State Department said on October 3 that Washington was concerned about indications that the Slovak government's commitment to democracy had been weakening. Hamzik denied that the United States had criticised Bratislava's treatment of minorities during his visit to Washington earlier this month.
Hamzik told the OSCE that Slovakia had embraced democracy, a market economy and adherence to human rights, but the process of change was continuing and was strengthening.
